match.reason: The closest bank card, geo-urbanisation, defines urbanisation and mentions pull factors but leaves out push factors like poverty and few jobs, and its questions test measurement rather than why it happens, so adding those would be a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Urbanisation and why it happens
card: Urbanisation is the growing share of a country's people who live in towns and cities. It is a change in the share, not just in the number of city dwellers.
things that drive people out of rural areas, such as poverty, few jobs, and farmland that can no longer support a family.
things that draw people to cities, such as paid work, services like hospitals, and schools and universities.
Push and pull factors often work together. A person may leave a farm because of low income and move to a city because jobs are on offer there.
draft.remember: Urbanisation is a rising share of people in cities. Push factors drive people out of rural areas and pull factors draw them to cities.

a.q: Which of these best describes urbanisation?
opts: A growing share of people living in towns and cities
A city spreading out over more land each year
More people being born in cities than in rural areas
Towns and cities being built with taller buildings
a.why: Urbanisation is about the share of a country's people who live in towns and cities. A city spreading over more land is a different thing, because it describes the size of the city and not where people live.
a.clue: Think about where people live, as a share of the whole country.

b.q: Sunita's family has farmed in rural India for years, but poor harvests have left them with little income. She moves to Pune to work in a hospital. Which pair correctly names the push and the pull?
opts: Push: poor harvests and low income. Pull: hospital work
Push: hospital work. Pull: poor harvests and low income
Push: poor harvests and low income. Pull: farming
Push: hospital work. Pull: living in the countryside
b.why: Poor harvests and low income drove Sunita out of her rural area, so they are push factors. The hospital job in Pune drew her to the city, so it is a pull factor. The second option swaps push and pull.
b.clue: Push drives people away from where they live. Pull draws them to a new place.

a.best: A growing share of people living in towns and cities

b.best: Push: poor harvests and low income. Pull: hospital work

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'The second option swaps push and pull', but options are shown in a random order. In the order shown, the second option is the correct one and the fourth is the swapped one, so this reference can mislead students.
The clue says to think about where people live 'as a share of the whole country'. Only the right option uses the word 'share', so a student can match the word without knowing the idea.
